intro: Lesson 18: Classifying living things: vertebrates, invertebrates and plants. To understand how living things are grouped by their features

blocks.title: Sort into: Vertebrate / Invertebrate
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Vertebrate, Invertebrate.
blocks.answer: Vertebrate: frog; eagle; shark; lizard. Invertebrate: snail; spider; earthworm; butterfly

head: Group
Key feature
Example
rows: fur or hair; feed young milk
moist skin; live in water and on land

questions.q: Is a spider a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
questions.a: An invertebrate: it has no backbone.
questions.model: Ask: does it have a backbone? A spider does not; it has a hard outer skeleton. No backbone means invertebrate.

questions.q: Is a fern a flowering plant?
questions.a: No, it is non-flowering (it makes spores).

questions.q: Core: Sort 12 living things (from the portal card set) into vertebrates (in their five groups), invertebrates and plants.
questions.a: Answers on the card set key, e.g. whale: mammal; frog: amphibian; snail: invertebrate; fern: non-flowering plant.
questions.model: Teacher sorts the first two: robin (feathers: bird), earthworm (no backbone: invertebrate).

questions.q: Extend: Why is a whale a mammal and not a fish?
questions.a: It breathes air with lungs and feeds its young milk.

questions.q: Stretch: Write three yes/no questions that would sort any vertebrate into its group.
questions.a: For example: Does it have feathers? Does it have fur? Does it have gills?

questions.q: An animal with a backbone is a...
Big question: is a snail more like a worm or like a fish?
questions.a: Like a worm: both are invertebrates with no backbone.
